subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Concorde: The Beautiful Engineering Compromise
description: A micro-lesson that makes Concorde: The Beautiful Engineering Compromise usable.

hook.text: Concorde flew London to New York in 3.5 hours at Mach 2. It was an engineering marvel that couldn't make money.

buildup.text: At Mach 2, air friction heated the airframe to 127 degrees Celsius. The fuselage expanded by 30 cm during flight.

discovery.text: The delta wing design generated enough lift at high speed but required very high landing speeds — over 180 mph.

twist.text: Sonic booms banned Concorde from overland supersonic flight. That limited it to transatlantic routes, killing its business case.

climax.text: Concorde retired in 2003 after 27 years. No supersonic airliner has replaced it. The economics never worked.

punchline.text: Faster than sound. Slower than profit. Engineering isn't just physics.

quiz.question: What limited Concorde's commercial success the most?
options: The aircraft could only carry 12 passengers due to weight restrictions
Sonic boom restrictions banned overland supersonic flight, limiting its routes
Engine reliability issues caused frequent cancellations and delays
